events.title: Gabriel Announces John’s Birth
events.description: While Zechariah offers incense in the sanctuary, Gabriel announces that Elizabeth will bear a son who will prepare Israel for the Lord. Because Zechariah doubts the message, he is unable to speak until its fulfillment.

events.title: Gabriel Announces Jesus’ Birth
events.description: Gabriel visits Mary in Nazareth and announces that she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear the promised Davidic ruler. Mary accepts the calling despite her initial perplexity.

events.title: Mary Visits Elizabeth
events.description: Mary travels to the Judean hill country, where Elizabeth recognizes the significance of her pregnancy. Mary praises God for overturning human status and remembering the covenant before returning home after about three months.

events.title: John Is Born and Named
events.description: Elizabeth gives birth, and at the child’s circumcision she and Zechariah insist on the name John. Zechariah’s speech returns, and he prophesies about God’s deliverance and his son’s work of preparation.

events.title: Jesus Is Born at Bethlehem
events.description: A registration brings Joseph and the pregnant Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem. Mary gives birth to her firstborn son and places him in a manger because ordinary lodging is unavailable.

events.title: Shepherds Visit the Newborn Jesus
events.description: Angels announce the child’s birth to shepherds watching nearby flocks. The shepherds find Mary, Joseph, and the infant, spread the news they received, and return praising God.

events.title: Jesus Is Presented in the Temple
events.description: After Jesus is circumcised and named, his parents present him in Jerusalem according to the law. Simeon and Anna recognize the child’s significance for Israel and the nations, and the family later returns to Nazareth.

events.title: The Boy Jesus Remains in the Temple
events.description: At age twelve Jesus remains in Jerusalem after Passover while his parents begin traveling home. They find him after three days among the temple teachers, and he then returns obediently to Nazareth and continues to mature.

events.title: John Calls the Jordan Region to Repentance
events.description: In Tiberius’s fifteenth year John proclaims a baptism of repentance, gives practical ethical directions to crowds, and announces a more powerful successor. Herod later imprisons him after John condemns the ruler’s wrongdoing.

events.title: Jesus Is Baptized and His Ancestry Recounted
events.description: As Jesus prays after baptism, the Spirit descends and a heavenly voice identifies him as the beloved Son. Luke then traces his ancestry through David and Abraham back to Adam and God.

events.title: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness
events.description: Filled with the Spirit, Jesus spends forty days in the wilderness and resists tests concerning food, political dominion, and a public display of divine protection.

events.title: Nazareth Rejects Jesus’ Mission
events.description: Jesus reads from Isaiah in his hometown synagogue and presents the passage as fulfilled in their hearing. When he recalls prophetic aid given to outsiders, the congregation attempts to kill him, but he escapes.

events.title: Jesus Teaches and Heals at Capernaum
events.description: Jesus expels a spirit in the synagogue, heals Simon’s feverish mother-in-law, and cures many who gather after sunset. He then departs to proclaim God’s kingdom in other towns.

events.title: A Great Catch Leads Fishermen to Follow Jesus
events.description: After teaching from Simon’s boat, Jesus directs the fishermen to a catch so large that two boats begin to sink. Simon, James, and John leave their work to follow him and gather people.

events.title: Jesus Cleanses a Leper and Heals a Paralytic
events.description: Jesus touches and cleanses a man with a skin disease, then forgives and heals a paralyzed man lowered through a roof. The second act provokes questions about his authority to forgive sins.

events.title: Jesus Calls Levi and Answers Critics
events.description: Levi leaves his tax booth and hosts a banquet for Jesus, prompting criticism over his company. Jesus describes his mission to sinners and uses wedding, garment, and wineskin images to answer a question about fasting.

events.title: Jesus Faces Sabbath Disputes
events.description: Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath and declares his authority over the day. On another Sabbath he restores a man’s withered hand while opponents begin considering action against him.

events.title: Jesus Chooses the Twelve and Teaches on a Plain
events.description: After a night of prayer Jesus names twelve apostles and heals people gathered from a wide region. He teaches about blessings and woes, love of enemies, generosity, judgment, character, and obedience.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Centurion’s Servant
events.description: Jewish elders appeal to Jesus for a Roman centurion’s gravely ill servant. The officer expresses confidence that Jesus can heal by command from a distance, and the servant recovers.

events.title: Jesus Raises a Widow’s Son at Nain
events.description: At Nain Jesus encounters the funeral of a widow’s only son. Moved by compassion, he stops the procession and restores the young man to life, prompting widespread reports.

events.title: Jesus Answers John’s Messengers
events.description: John sends disciples to ask about Jesus’ identity, and Jesus directs them to the healings and proclamation they have witnessed. He then honors John’s prophetic role and exposes the generation’s inconsistent rejection of them both.

events.title: A Woman Anoints Jesus at a Pharisee’s Table
events.description: At Simon the Pharisee’s meal, a woman known as a sinner washes and anoints Jesus’ feet. Through a story of canceled debts, Jesus contrasts her grateful love with the host’s reception and confirms her forgiveness.

events.title: Women Support Jesus’ Proclamation Tour
events.description: Jesus travels through towns and villages proclaiming God’s kingdom with the twelve. Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna, and other women accompany the group and provide from their resources.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Hearing God’s Word
events.description: Jesus tells and explains the parable of seed falling on four kinds of ground, then adds instruction about bringing light into view. When his relatives seek him, he defines his family as those who hear and obey God’s word.

events.title: Jesus Calms a Storm and Frees a Gerasene Man
events.description: Jesus stills a dangerous storm during a lake crossing. On the opposite shore he drives many demons from a tormented man into pigs, and sends the restored man home to report what God has done.

events.title: A Woman Is Healed and Jairus’s Daughter Raised
events.description: A woman suffering twelve years is healed after touching Jesus while he travels to Jairus’s house. Although word arrives that Jairus’s daughter has died, Jesus restores the girl to life.

events.title: The Twelve Are Sent and Five Thousand Are Fed
events.description: Jesus sends the twelve to announce the kingdom and heal with little travel equipment. After their return he welcomes a crowd near Bethsaida and feeds about five thousand men with five loaves and two fish.

events.title: Peter Confesses Jesus and Three Disciples See His Glory
events.description: Peter identifies Jesus as God’s Messiah, after which Jesus predicts his rejection, death, and resurrection and defines costly discipleship. About eight days later his appearance changes on a mountain as Moses and Elijah speak with him.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Boy and Corrects the Disciples
events.description: Jesus frees a boy after the disciples fail to do so and again foretells his betrayal. He counters their dispute about greatness with a child and tells them not to stop an outsider expelling demons in his name.

events.title: Jesus Sets Out for Jerusalem
events.description: Jesus decisively begins the journey toward Jerusalem. He rebukes disciples who want to punish an unreceptive Samaritan village and warns would-be followers about the journey’s demands.

events.title: Seventy Disciples Are Sent and Return
events.description: Jesus sends seventy disciples in pairs to heal and announce God’s approaching kingdom. They return joyful at their authority over spirits, and Jesus redirects their joy toward belonging to God.

events.title: Jesus Tells the Parable of the Good Samaritan
events.description: When a legal expert asks how to inherit life and who qualifies as a neighbor, Jesus describes a robbed traveler ignored by religious figures but aided generously by a Samaritan. He directs the questioner to practice the same mercy.

events.title: Martha Welcomes Jesus as Mary Listens
events.description: Martha hosts Jesus but becomes distracted by serving while her sister Mary listens at his feet. Jesus affirms Mary’s attention to his teaching as the better priority.

events.title: Jesus Teaches His Disciples to Pray
events.description: Jesus gives his disciples a pattern of prayer centered on God’s name, kingdom, provision, forgiveness, and deliverance. A story about a persistent friend and comparisons with parental generosity encourage confident persistence.

events.title: Jesus Answers Opponents and Denounces Hypocrisy
events.description: After an exorcism Jesus refutes claims that his power comes from the ruler of demons and rejects demands for a sign beyond Jonah’s. At a Pharisee’s meal he pronounces woes against outward piety, neglected justice, and burdensome religious leadership.

events.title: Jesus Warns Against Hypocrisy and Greed
events.description: Jesus urges fearless public faithfulness and warns that possessions do not secure life. The parable of a rich landowner whose life ends after he enlarges his barns leads into teaching about trust, generosity, and heavenly treasure.

events.title: Jesus Calls for Watchful Service
events.description: Through images of waiting servants, a thief, and a responsible manager, Jesus urges readiness and faithful stewardship. He also warns that his mission will expose division and calls the crowds to recognize the present moment.

events.title: Jesus Calls for Repentance and Heals a Bent Woman
events.description: Jesus rejects the idea that victims of violence or disaster were uniquely sinful and tells of an unfruitful fig tree given more time. In a synagogue he frees a woman disabled for eighteen years and defends healing her on the Sabbath.

events.title: Jesus Teaches on the Narrow Door and Laments Jerusalem
events.description: Traveling toward Jerusalem, Jesus warns that familiarity does not replace entering God’s kingdom and foresees people arriving from every direction. He refuses intimidation by Herod and laments Jerusalem’s rejection of God’s messengers.

events.title: Jesus Heals and Teaches at a Pharisee’s Dinner
events.description: Jesus heals a man with edema on the Sabbath and silences objections. Observing the meal, he teaches humility and generous hospitality, then tells of invited guests whose excuses lead a host to fill his banquet with marginalized people.

events.title: Jesus Describes the Cost of Discipleship
events.description: Jesus tells the traveling crowds that following him requires loyalty beyond family ties, acceptance of the cross, and surrender of possessions. Images of an unfinished tower and an outmatched king stress deliberate commitment.

events.title: Jesus Tells Three Parables About the Lost
events.description: Responding to criticism that he welcomes sinners, Jesus tells of a recovered sheep, a recovered coin, and a wayward son welcomed by his father. Each story emphasizes joy over restoration while the elder son’s resentment mirrors the critics.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Wealth and Faithfulness
events.description: A parable about a dishonest but shrewd manager leads to teaching on faithful use of wealth and undivided service to God. Jesus then contrasts a rich man’s luxury with poor Lazarus’s suffering and their reversed conditions after death.

events.title: Jesus Cleanses Ten People with Leprosy
events.description: After teaching about forgiveness, faith, and humble obedience, Jesus cleanses ten people while traveling between Samaria and Galilee. Only a Samaritan returns to thank him and praise God.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Kingdom and the Son of Man
events.description: Jesus tells Pharisees that God’s kingdom is already among them rather than arriving through easily observed signs. He warns disciples that the Son of Man’s revelation will be sudden and will follow suffering and rejection.

events.title: Jesus Tells Parables About Persistent and Humble Prayer
events.description: A persistent widow eventually receives justice from an unjust judge, encouraging continued prayer. A second story contrasts a self-satisfied Pharisee with a tax collector who humbly seeks mercy.

events.title: Jesus Welcomes Children and Challenges a Rich Ruler
events.description: Jesus welcomes infants whom the disciples try to prevent from approaching and presents childlike reception as necessary for the kingdom. A wealthy ruler grieves when told to distribute his property and follow, prompting teaching about wealth and salvation.

events.title: Jesus Predicts His Death and Heals a Blind Man
events.description: Jesus privately tells the twelve that he will be abused, killed, and raised in Jerusalem, though they do not understand. Near Jericho he restores sight to a persistent blind beggar who then follows him.

events.title: Jesus Stays with Zacchaeus
events.description: At Jericho Jesus calls the wealthy chief tax collector Zacchaeus down from a tree and stays at his house. Zacchaeus promises substantial generosity and restitution, and Jesus declares that restoration has reached the household.

events.title: Jesus Tells the Parable of the Ten Pounds
events.description: Because listeners expect God’s kingdom to appear immediately near Jerusalem, Jesus describes a nobleman who departs to receive royal authority. On returning, he rewards servants who traded entrusted money and judges resistance and inactivity.

events.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem and Clears the Temple
events.description: Jesus rides toward Jerusalem on a colt amid his disciples’ praise, then weeps over the city and foretells its siege. He drives sellers from the temple and teaches there daily while leaders seek to kill him.

events.title: Jesus Answers an Authority Challenge and Warns Leaders
events.description: When leaders demand the source of his authority, Jesus asks whether John’s baptism came from heaven or human beings. He then tells of tenants who kill a vineyard owner’s son, and the leaders recognize the warning against them.

events.title: Jesus Answers Temple Debates
events.description: Jesus avoids a trap about imperial taxes by distinguishing obligations to the emperor and to God. He answers Sadducees about resurrection, questions assumptions about David’s son, and warns against scribes who pursue honor while exploiting widows.

events.title: Jesus Observes a Widow and Foretells the Temple’s Fall
events.description: Jesus highlights a poor widow’s small offering as greater than gifts from abundance. He predicts the temple’s destruction, persecution, Jerusalem’s distress, and the Son of Man’s coming, urging alertness and endurance.

events.title: Judas Arranges to Betray Jesus
events.description: As leaders seek a way to kill Jesus without provoking the crowd, Judas agrees to betray him for money. Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the Passover meal in an upstairs room.

events.title: Jesus Shares the Last Supper
events.description: At Passover Jesus gives bread and a cup to interpret his approaching death and identifies a betrayer at the table. He corrects the apostles’ rivalry, foretells Peter’s denials, and prepares them for the coming crisis.

events.title: Jesus Prays and Is Arrested on the Mount of Olives
events.description: Jesus prays in anguish while his disciples sleep, submitting his will to the Father. Judas leads an armed group to arrest him, and Jesus heals the high priest’s servant after a disciple cuts off his ear.

events.title: Peter Denies Jesus and the Council Questions Him
events.description: Peter follows to the high priest’s house but denies knowing Jesus three times and leaves weeping after the rooster crows. Jesus’ captors mock him, and at daybreak the council questions him about being Messiah and Son of God.

events.title: Pilate and Herod Examine Jesus Before His Sentence
events.description: The council accuses Jesus before Pilate, who sends the Galilean to Herod and receives him back after mockery. Though Pilate repeatedly finds no capital offense, the crowd’s demand prevails, Barabbas is released, and Jesus is handed over.

events.title: Jesus Is Crucified and Dies
events.description: Simon of Cyrene carries the cross as Jesus is led to the place of execution with two criminals. Jesus is crucified between them; darkness covers the land, the temple curtain tears, and he dies as followers watch from a distance.

events.title: Joseph Buries Jesus
events.description: Joseph of Arimathea receives Jesus’ body and places it in a previously unused rock-cut tomb before the Sabbath. The Galilean women observe the location, prepare burial spices, and rest on the Sabbath.

events.title: Women Find the Tomb Empty
events.description: At dawn on the first day of the week, women find the stone moved and Jesus’ body absent. Two heavenly messengers announce his resurrection; the apostles initially dismiss the report, but Peter runs to inspect the tomb.

events.title: The Risen Jesus Appears on the Emmaus Road
events.description: Jesus joins two grieving disciples traveling to Emmaus, explains the scriptures concerning the Messiah, and remains unrecognized until breaking bread with them. They immediately return to Jerusalem to report the encounter.

events.title: The Risen Jesus Appears to the Gathered Disciples
events.description: Jesus appears among the gathered disciples, shows them his hands and feet, and eats fish to assure them that he is bodily present. He opens their understanding of scripture and commissions worldwide proclamation beginning in Jerusalem.

events.title: Jesus Ascends Near Bethany
events.description: Jesus leads the disciples toward Bethany, blesses them, and is carried into heaven. They worship him, return joyfully to Jerusalem, and continue praising God in the temple.
